Resolves #45

Syncs `Docs.view.MainContainerController` theme and source-view theme button texts (`theme-button`, `source-view-theme-button`) and the initial HighlightJS stylesheet path to `me.component.getTheme()` in `onComponentConstructed()`, hides `theme-button` when embedded inside the Portal (`appName === 'Portal'`), and removes the obsolete `theme: 'neo-theme-light'` override from `Docs.view.MainContainer` so standalone and embedded Docs views oppose their active boot theme on first render without overwriting the Portal's `document.body` theme (Contract Ledger: [`IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABilNeDQ`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/45#issuecomment-6615686669)).

`agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline lint-staged + unit tests ran` (`--change-class capability`).

Evidence: L2 (Playwright unit spec driving `Docs.view.MainContainer` across standalone and embedded Portal configurations) → L2 required (theme and source-view theme button texts adjust to oppose the initial theme).

## AC Evidence
No structured ACs on #45.

| Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Theme and source-view theme button texts adjust to oppose the theme the app started with, publish body theme only when standalone, and hide the Docs theme button inside the Portal | `test/playwright/unit/apps/docs/view/MainContainerController.spec.mjs` (`adjusts theme and source-view theme button texts to oppose the initial theme, publishes body theme only when standalone, and hides the Docs theme button inside the Portal`) |

## Deltas from ticket
- Removed the temporary `theme: 'neo-theme-light'` override from `docs/app/view/MainContainer.mjs` (superseded once `resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/apps/docs/` and `resources/scss/theme-neo-light/apps/docs/` landed) so `getTheme()` resolves the inherited Portal theme when embedded or `Neo.config.themes[0]` when standalone, which also stops the embedded `Docs.view.MainContainer` (`Viewport` subclass) from publishing `neo-theme-light` onto the Portal's `document.body` at construct (`Viewport#onConstructed` → `syncBodyTheme`).
- Hid `theme-button` when `appName === 'Portal'` so the Portal header's theme switch remains the single owner of the Portal page and `document.body` theme while `source-view-theme-button` continues to sync and toggle HighlightJS stylesheets under `../../docs/resources/lib/`.
- Removed redundant manual `view.cls` mutation from `onSwitchThemeButtonClick()` so `component.Base#afterSetTheme` is the sole owner of the theme carrier class.

## Test Evidence
All coverage runs in CI.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] None required; all assertions run in CI unit tests.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: `Docs.view.MainContainer` extends `container.Viewport`. Since #18599 (13.3.1), a viewport with `applyBodyCls: true` (the default) mirrors its effective theme onto `document.body`. The Viewport docblock assumes a top-level view, and nothing marks the Portal's embedded Docs view as nested, so it becomes a second body publisher in the Portal window. *Hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation:* other viewports embedded in the Portal may publish the same way. *   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: N/A
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: A theme fix inside an embeddable app has three surfaces: the view's own theme class, the theme it inherits from its host, and the body it may publish to. A plain `Container` stand-in in the spec reaches only the first.

### 📋 Required Actions

To proceed with merging, please address the following:

- [ ] **RA-1 — a Docs theme click inside the Portal must not change the Portal's `document.body` theme.**
    - Why it does today: `Docs.view.MainContainer` is a `container.Viewport` (`applyBodyCls: true` by default), so the new `view.theme = theme` runs `Viewport#afterSetTheme` → `syncBodyTheme`. Each click replaces the Portal's theme on the body with the Docs-local one (probe row 2).
    - Recommended route: the Portal header's switch owns the page theme. The embedded Docs view hides its theme button and simply inherits (the controller already branches on `appName === 'Portal'`). The source-view button stays, with its boot sync as you have it.
    - Alternative, if you keep a Docs-local toggle in the Portal, three things are needed:
        - The Portal's Docs item must not publish (`applyBodyCls: false` on it).
        - The scoped theme's text colour needs a visual check: `container/Viewport.scss` sets only `background-color` on `.neo-viewport`, and the `syncBodyTheme` docblock records inherited text at 1.13:1 contrast.
        - Both labels and the toggle direction must follow a host theme switch. Key the direction on `getTheme()`, as `Portal.view.ViewportController#onSwitchTheme` does, rather than on the label's text (rows 3-4).
    - Either way, name the body-theme change in the PR body's deltas.
- [ ] **RA-2 — one owner for the theme class.** In `onSwitchThemeButtonClick`, drop the manual `cls` filter/add and set `view.theme` alone. `component.Base#afterSetTheme` already removes the old carrier class and adds the new one, so the method currently runs two owners of one class through chained direct writes on a live instance.
- [ ] **RA-3 — the spec drives the real Viewport subclass.** The new case builds a plain `Container`, so the path RA-1 lives on never runs in it.
    - Setup: use `Docs.view.MainContainer` embedded in a host, with `Neo.main.DomAccess.setBodyCls` and `applyBodyCls` stubbed and recorded. The probe above runs in the unit env with `src/manager/Instance.mjs` imported.
    - Assertions: RA-1's outcome in the embedded arm. Keep a standalone arm, where publishing to the body is correct because the Docs view is the top-level viewport there.
